title: Hear our prayer
hookLine: here any personal request may be added in your own words

lines: AS FIXED AS A PRAYER GETS.
WHAT IF IT'S NOT ON THE LIST?
cards: The Amidah's words are fixed. Jews in Tokyo and Toronto say nearly the same sentences, in the same order, three times a day. Which raises a fair question.
What if what you actually need isn't on the list? A scholarship. The courage to leave a bad job.
Your dog's surgery on Thursday. A sister who hasn't called back. The prayer has an answer for that, and it's built into the very last request.

teach.b: The sixteenth blessing says: hear our voice, Lord our God. Have pity and compassion on us, and accept our prayer with mercy and favor.
Don't turn us away empty-handed, for You hear the prayer of every mouth. Blessed are You, who hears prayer. In Hebrew, shome'a tefillah.
The Psalms put it this way, in the old Jewish translation: "O Thou that hearest prayer, unto Thee doth all flesh come." All flesh. Every mouth.
Not only the eloquent, not only those who know the Hebrew. The Talmud, in Avodah Zarah 8a, records the rule: a person may ask for their own needs in this blessing.

teach.h: ANY NEED MAY BE ADDED HERE.
teach.b: Any need. The fixed requests before it cover what a whole people needs: wisdom, forgiveness, healing, a good year, justice. This one leaves a gap for what only you need.
And it doesn't have to be in Hebrew.

The Mishnah already allows the Amidah to be said in any language a person understands, and personal additions are often whispered in whatever language the heart speaks first: English, Yiddish, Spanish, Russian, Amharic.
Someone fasting privately adds a short prayer here too. It's like a long printed form that ends with one open box: anything else?
The tradition holds the words steady for everyone, and then, near the end, steps back and says: now, in your own words.

how: Shome'a tefillah is the sixteenth blessing of the weekday Amidah; many Jews pause within it to add personal requests in their own words and language, and someone keeping a private fast adds the prayer Aneinu here.

games.q: your best friend's surgery is on Thursday. it's not on the Amidah's printed list. what can you do?
o: add it in your own words in shome'a tefillah.
games.why: Avodah Zarah 8a: a person may ask for any need in shome'a tefillah, in their own words.

practice: Ask yourself what you actually need right now, not what you think you should need, and let it be specific, even a little embarrassing: the exam, the bill, the conversation you're dreading, the loneliness on Sunday nights.
Put it into one plain sentence, in whatever language comes first. If you pray, say it as a request; if not, simply say it to yourself, under your breath.
